summary: Persistent sporadic 5xx correlated with proxy handoff latency and runtime SIGTERM churn
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (OpenFinch Labs) reports intermittent 5xx responses when sending mixed chat+embedding requests at sustained rates (~250 rps) to the hosted API. Errors manifest as short spikes of 502/503 and occasional runtime exits on upstream workers. Problem started 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC and recurred during evening traffic windows.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints returning 502/503 for 30s-3m windows.
- Customer reports degraded UX and increased retries.
- A subset of upstream runtimes report SIGTERM then restart loops.

Environment:
- prod - us-west
- Customer on Dedicated pool tenant ID: ofl-dedicated-71
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embeddings/batch

Steps to reproduce (observed at scale):
1) Send mixed workload from same client: 60% streaming chat sessions, 40% embeddings bulk upload (batch size 64).
2) Traffic ramp to ~200-300 rps over 2 minutes.
3) Observe proxy connection handoff latency increasing (long TCP/TLS setup times).
4) Upstream runtime processes receive SIGTERM and restart; 502/503s spike during this period.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpts):
- api-gateway logs: "2026-03-09T23:12:41Z proxy: handoff latency=789ms route=/v1/chat/stream tenant=ofl-dedicated-71"
- proxy logs: "handoff delayed, queue_depth=87, accept_wait=421ms"
- runtime syslog: "2026-03-09T23:12:44Z runtime[pid=2145]: Received SIGTERM, reason=parent_graceful_shutdown"
- runtime exit reason: "watchdog: preemption timeout during kernel swap"
- customer-reported: spike started ~23:10 UTC and repeated 23:30-23:40 UTC during their evening jobs.

Hypotheses so far:
- Proxy handoff latency (accept queue/backpressure) causes graceful shutdown logic in the runtime to fire (SIGTERM) while worker is still handling long-lived streaming connections, producing a cascade of exits and 502/503s.
- Noisy embedding bulk uploads are pushing accept-queue depth and causing large tail latencies; combined with tight graceful shutdown timeouts this leads to churn.
- Potential misalignment between proxy backpressure thresholds and runtime graceful shutdown thresholds (race condition).

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Rolled out a temporary accept-queue throttle bump on the tenant route for ofl-dedicated-71 at 2026-03-10T02:15 UTC (increased conn backlog limit + extended handshake timeouts).
- Suggested customer reduce embedding batch size to 16 as a short-term workaround.

Next steps:
- SRE to verify proxy -> runtime threshold alignment and increase graceful shutdown window for affected pool.
- Engineering to validate runtime shutdown logic under backpressure and check for stray SIGTERM triggers during kernel swaps.
- Ask customer to run reduced-batch test and report if 5xx stops.

Related artifacts:
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/ofl-dedicated-71/acceptqueue
- Incidents / runbooks referenced: CON-acceptqueue-backpressure-runbook
comments: Support - 2026-03-10: Maya Patel: Acknowledged report and triaged. Informed customer we are prioritizing as P1. Requested pprof traces and runtime logs for the 23:10 window.

SRE - 2026-03-10: Aaron Li: Observed repeated accept_queue spikes for tenant ofl-dedicated-71 matching customer's timestamps. Queues peaked at ~120, avg handoff latency >700ms. Increased backlog soft limit on edge proxy as stopgap. Gathering kernel swap telemetry.

Engineering - 2026-03-11: Priya Desai: Preliminary debug indicates graceful_shutdown() path receives SIGTERM due to autoscaler preemption combined with proxy perceiving the worker as unhealthy (handshake timeouts). Propose: extend grace window by 6s and add hysteresis on preempt decisions during heavy-accept-queue pressure.
Customer - 2026-03-11: Jordan Hale (OpenFinch): Confirmed reduced batch size to 16 eliminated 5xx spikes in a 2-hour test window. Requested ETA for permanent fix and prevention for other tenants.

SRE - 2026-03-12: Ethan Brooks: Implemented canary with extended graceful shutdown + adjusted preempt hysteresis on 2 nodes in the pool. Monitoring for 48 hours. Initial signals show acceptqueue depth still high but no SIGTERM cascade after change.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: canary deployment extended graceful shutdown + preempt hysteresis. Customer workaround validated (reduced embedding batch size). Follow-up: engineering to harden runtime shutdown logic and add metrics to trace handoff latency -> shutdown triggers. Postmortem to be scheduled after 48h validation.
